input.quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
input.rationale: Section 13 contains an express Garman non-infringement warranty backed by an indemnity in our favour covering Losses (including settlement amounts and legal fees) and the usual remedy ladder of procuring rights, substituting an equivalent element, or replacing/modifying the Work (p0090–p0093). There is no reverse indemnity from Sparkling anywhere in the agreement, so the walk-away scenario does not arise, and Section 15 expressly carves breaches of Section 13 out of the liability cap and consequential-damages exclusion, which is better than the fallback's 3x super-cap. This therefore sits at (and in the cap respect above) the fallback position and is not redlined. Noted for information only, short of the preferred position: there is no express "defend"/control-of-defence mechanic, no refund remedy if none of (a)-(c) is achievable, the indemnity is limited to IP/title matters (no breach of law, data breach or gross negligence/wilful misconduct limbs), affiliates are not named, and the ten-calendar-day notice requirement is tight — we would take these in negotiation but they are sub-elements rather than fallback failures.
